title: DSH trusted-local acceptance specification (Windows, no sandbox)

supersedes.note: This file does NOT modify or replace qualification/specs/acceptance-spec.json. The old spec stays on disk, immutable, as history. This is a NEW spec under a NEW deployment identity.

trust_model.name: trusted-local
trust_model.one_line: The OS user account is the execution authority boundary.
trust_model.statement: DSH runs as the invoking Windows user with no sandbox, no WSL, no Linux VM and no SSH execution world. Every process it starts -- including the IPython kernel -- runs as that same OS user with that user's full filesystem, network and process visibility. This deployment therefore claims NO confinement of reads, writes, network or process visibility, and no case in this spec may be read as establishing one. What this deployment does claim is bounded and checkable: identity, composition, one programmable execution surface, correct data and recovery behaviour, bounded concurrency, honest verification, and research provenance.
explicitly_not_claimed: host-secret read isolation (any process can read any file the OS user can read)
network / egress isolation (there is no OS or gateway boundary)
filesystem write confinement (danger-full-access means no write restriction either)
a second execution world, and therefore any cross-world path consistency or role transition
verification-environment privilege separation from the host
trust_model.sandbox_rows_retained_because: The pinned DSH ABI requires them. `sandboxPolicy` is a SERVICE that seven entries inject, and `inject` is a readiness gate: deleting the row leaves those entries permanently pending, cascades so that shell/fs/ptcRuntime never publish, and the preset fails to mount with the model's tool face at ZERO. MEASURED. The rows are therefore configured as `danger-full-access`, which is DSH's own first-class path (ConfinedSandboxMode EXCLUDES it by type).
trust_model.identity_boundary: compatibility.lock.json -> deployment.identity. Every case below is bound to that identity. A PASS recorded against another identity is not a PASS for this one.

ROOT'S RE-MEASUREMENT of IPY-13's two clauses, together with CAP-10, from the full serial suite run of the integrated candidate. Both clauses are printed by the project's own v3-spec-gates test as structured [V3-MEASURED] lines, so the numbers are the product's, not a re-derivation.

cases.note: FAIL on the LITERAL second clause, and the correction is recorded because an earlier version of this note read PASS. WHAT THE ORACLE REQUIRES, verbatim: 'The post-return write is reported as late/unattributed and does not appear in any later cell's result. A write landing DURING a later cell is reported as UNDECIDABLE rather than attributed. A claim that the originating cell's parent id is always preserved is NOT PASS, because it is false for a thread started with an empty context.' WHAT IS MEASURED (writer c7's independent class probe, qualification/results/C7-remeasure/ipy13-class-probe.json -- NOT the v3-spec-gates gate, which is the point): (a) CLAUSE 1 HOLDS. A post-return write is delivered as a late record with causalClass 'known-late', it carries the originating cell id, and it appears in no later cell's result. (b) THE SUBSTANTIVE HALF OF CLAUSE 2 HOLDS. The straddler -- a write landing while a later cell runs -- is NOT folded into that later cell. Cell B's stdout is exactly its own ticks ('tick 0..3') with cellBContainsStraddler false, and the write is delivered separately as a runtime notice naming its origin cell. The recorded defect (the marker appearing inside the later cell's stdout with lateCount 0) is measurably GONE. (c) THE LITERAL HALF OF CLAUSE 2 DOES NOT HOLD. The straddler is classified 'known-late', not 'undecidable'. The probe disambiguates this by printing each cell's own msg_id: the recorded origin is cell A's '..._39380_5', and cell B is '..._39380_7', so originIsLaterCellB is false and originIsOriginatingCellA is true. The notice text the model sees says 'background output from earlier cell(s)' and 'origin cell: ..._39380_5' -- it names a cell. The oracle's word is 'undecidable', and the product's word is 'known-late'. WHY THE EARLIER PASS WAS WRONG, stated plainly because it is this project's most-recorded defect class. The v3-spec-gates test that reported 'clause_met' asserts only that the write was not attributed to the later cell. It NEVER asserts the causal class. So a green there is an oracle WEAKER THAN ITS SCENARIO: it confirms the property the product has and skips the property the spec names. Writer c7 closed that gap with a probe that prints the class, and the class is not the one the oracle requires. Marking this PASS on the strength of the weaker gate would have been exactly the substitution this project's rules forbid. THE PRODUCT'S BEHAVIOUR IS ARGUABLY BETTER THAN THE ORACLE ASKS, and that does not make the case PASS. The product distinguishes two situations the oracle collapses into one: when the bootstrap carried the originating cell's header into a cell-started thread, the origin IS preserved and the write is reported 'known-late' with a true cell id; when a raw thread carries no identity ('UNDECIDABLE (recorded origin dsh:background)'), it is reported undecidable. Preserving a true origin is a stronger answer than declaring undecidable -- but the oracle names 'undecidable' as the required outcome, and an oracle is not satisfied by a better outcome it did not anticipate. The oracle's THIRD sentence is also respected and is worth noting: the product does NOT claim the parent id is always preserved, and the raw-thread arm is the evidence that it does not. RESOLUTION OWNED BY THE DELIVERY, recorded rather than taken: either this clause is a SPEC CLARITY defect (the oracle should require 'not attributed to the later cell, with a true origin when one is knowable, and undecidable otherwise'), or the product should report the straddler as undecidable. Choosing the first requires superseding the spec, which invalidates every verdict filed under the current identity -- a deliberate step, not a fix. Until that decision is made, the literal clause does not hold and this case stays FAIL. CLOSING NOTE ON WHAT DID CHANGE: the recorded defect is gone. This FAIL is about a WORD, and the note says so rather than presenting it as a product regression.

cases.requirement: a scan watermark is stable while events append
cases.stimulus: Run a history scan while new events keep being appended.
cases.oracle: The page order is fixed to one snapshot for the whole scan, and events appended after the snapshot are read in a separate pass with their own watermark. Interleaving new events into the running scan is NOT PASS.

evidence.note: T2 boot probe result: obs02WatermarkPinned -- the pinned watermark, the first page, the appended seqs, the continuation's watermark and seqs, and the four boolean facts (pinnedScanExcludedAppended, watermarkUnchangedAcrossPages, reopenedSeesAppended, generationAdvanced). The file also carries the home assertion and the build digest.
T2 driver transcript: rebuild exit 0, fresh profile installed (patch sha256 5b8b2a8e...), boot port 7322, portReleased true, probe named the booted home.

The HIS-02 block at T1: a pinned scan excludes appended events and a separate scan reads them at a new generation; at most ONE pinned observation per session; a superseded generation refused; page order stable across a filtered multi-page traversal.

cases.note: A scan is pinned to ONE watermark for its whole life, and events appended after the snapshot are read in a SEPARATE pass with their own watermark. MEASURED inside the booted composed host through the LOADED ctx.dailyHistory service: the scan pinned at {maxSeq 2, generation 1} and returned [0]; five events at seq 3..7 were then appended through the real persistence handle; the continuation returned [1,2] with exhausted true and pinnedScanExcludedAppended true; the watermark did NOT move across pages (maxSeq AND generation both identical, watermarkUnchangedAcrossPages true); and a fresh scan read {maxSeq 7, generation 2} with reopenedSeesAppended true and generationAdvanced true. So the new events came from a separate pass with their own watermark rather than being interleaved into the running one. The refusal direction is measured too: a superseded cursor is refused with HISTORY_WATERMARK_SUPERSEDED rather than re-based, including after closeScan and after dispose.

cases.requirement: one oversized event does not break the page budget
cases.stimulus: Read a history page containing a single event larger than the page budget.
cases.oracle: An authorized reference or a segmented read is returned, and the page budget is not exceeded. Truncating silently, or emitting the whole event inline, is NOT PASS.

evidence.note: T2 boot probe result: obs03OversizedEvent -- kind, totalBytes, the four segments, the digest check, complete, recovery, the no-body assertion, the segment-list bound, and the two-arm digest/byte agreement.
T2 driver transcript for that probe.

The HIS-03 block at T1: segments with the FULL size and digest and never a partial body as the event; the segment LIST bounded as well as each segment; an absent seq reported as an error rather than an empty event; and a digest stable across key ordering.

cases.note: An oversized event returns an authorized reference or a segmented read, and the page budget is not exceeded. MEASURED in the booted host on a 200,000-character event read with maxBytes 4096: kind 'segments', totalBytes 200203, 4 segments of 4096 bytes each, a hex64 digest OF THE FULL EVENT, complete false, recovery 'authorized-refetch', and NO field carrying the event body in this arm. The budget is enforced twice over: each segment is within the requested budget, and the segment LIST is capped, so a tiny budget against a huge event cannot return thousands of offsets -- which would be the same breach counted in a different unit. The two arms describe the SAME object: a second read at a larger budget returns kind 'value' whose digest equals the segments arm's digest and whose byte count equals its totalBytes. Nothing is silently truncated and the whole event is never emitted inline.

cases.requirement: repeated traversal does not re-replay the whole log
cases.stimulus: Traverse the same history for 100 pages.
cases.oracle: A prepared observation or index is reused, and the actual number of full log replays is recorded as a number. A measured 100 replays for 100 pages is reported as the defect it is.

evidence.note: The HIS-04 block at T1: the 100-page traversal at ONE log read with pages == 100, the counter's control arm (a second pinned scan increments it), and the byte-level measurement that distinguishes a pin from a per-page re-read.
T2 boot probe result: obs04Replay -- pages, exhausted, the materialization count for the traversal, the control arm's cost, and the per-session replay map.
T2 driver transcript for that probe, including the boot's port release and the installed-patch digest.

cases.note: A prepared observation is reused across a multi-page traversal, and the number of full log replays is recorded as a NUMBER, with a control arm that shows the counter is not a constant. MEASURED at T1 on a 500-event log through a persistence handle that counts every read: a 100-page traversal cost logReads 1 and replayCounter().total 1, with pages == 100 and every seq seen exactly once. The BYTES arm rules out a cache that still copies the whole log per page: ~500 KB read in total, bytesRead < oneLog * 1.5 and < 1 MB, where a per-page replay of the same log would be ~50 MB. CONFIRMED in the booted composed host at T2: a 9-page traversal of the stored session (9 events, exhausted true) cost fullLogMaterializationsForTheTraversal 1. THE CONTROL: a SECOND pinned scan of the same session costs a second materialization (controlArmSecondScanCost 1, controlHasTeeth true; the T1 file pins the same control as total 1 -> 2), so the 1 above is a measurement rather than a constant.

cases.requirement: the three visibilities stay separate
cases.stimulus: Store an event without reading it programmatically, then read it without emitting it, then emit it.
cases.oracle: `obtainable`, `consumed` and `model-projected` are recorded as three separate states and are never merged into one. Reporting a stored event as model-visible, or a consumed event as projected, is NOT PASS.

evidence.note: T2 boot probe result: obs05Visibilities -- the stored count and surfaces, the consumed and projected sets, the report, the disjointness and union checks, and the refusal measured on the loaded ledger. The same file's `reach` block records the model tool names, the ipython service's method list and the dailyHistory method list.

The HIS-05 block at T1: DSH's own three surfaces classified, consumption and projection recorded separately, refusal to record consumption for an event never stored, refusal to record projection for an event never consumed, and surface-filtered paging.

The reach measurement: 147 source files scanned under two named roots, per-module importer lists split into production / qualification-runner / test, and the dailyHistory caller table showing ZERO product callers of .history(...).

cases.note: Obtainable, consumed and model-projected are recorded as three SEPARATE states and are never merged. MEASURED in the booted host on the loaded plane's own records: 9 stored events, seq 0 recorded as consumed and then as projected, and the report yields storedOnly [1..8], consumedNotProjected [] and projected [0] -- three disjoint sets whose union accounts for every stored event. The refusal direction is measured on the loaded ledger: recording a projection for a seq that was never consumed throws HISTORY_EVENT_ABSENT, so 'the model saw it' cannot be inferred from 'it exists'. At T1 the classification uses DSH's OWN three-valued surface vocabulary rather than a second mechanism: a real compaction-style surfaceOp replace yields [0,'shadowed'],[1,'shadowed'],[2,'current'],[3,'current'], and the plane's surface filter pages by 'shadowed' and 'current' through session-query's own types. RECORDED IN THIS CASE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD AND NOT A FALSE PASS: the PRODUCT has ZERO callers of ctx.dailyHistory.history(caller) -- the service is mounted and serves authorized reads, but no model-facing tool, no Python-cell binding and no broker message type reaches it (BrokerOpName is [start, execute, interrupt, restart, shutdown, status, kernel_info]; BrokerEvent is [kernel_exited, late_output, diagnostic]; neither carries a host-callback or tool-call member). That is a gap in REACH, not a defect in the three visibilities.

cases.requirement: a derived index is rebuildable from canonical data
cases.stimulus: Delete the derived full-text index, then restore.
cases.oracle: The index is rebuilt from the canonical Session and artifact data with no second history source required, and the rebuilt index answers the same queries as before. The rebuild is recorded with what it read.

evidence.note: The standalone probe output: the baseline result, the index directory's contents before deletion and its absence after, the surviving canonical root and its enumerated contents, the rebuilt result, and the explicit same-answer verdict.
The probe itself, so a reader can re-run it: real SessionStore, real JSONL persistence, real SQLite FTS5 engine, with the deletion and the fresh boot in the middle.

The HIS-08 block at T1: an in-memory derived index dropped and rebuilt from canonical sessions, the REAL SQLite FTS index rebuilt after deleting its file, and the assertion that the index holds nothing the canonical logs lack.

cases.note: A derived index is rebuilt from canonical Session data with no second history source, and the rebuilt index answers the same query. MEASURED against the REAL SQLite FTS5 backend over the REAL JSONL persistence: the baseline query returned one session (id v10-obs06-session, bestMatchSeq 0, the marker present in the excerpt); the index directory was then DELETED -- all three files including the -wal and -shm -- and confirmed gone; a fresh engine was booted over the surviving session root; and the identical query returned the identical session id, seq and excerpt, so the answer was reconstructed rather than cached. WHAT IT READ is recorded rather than asserted: the canonical session root enumerated to its single session's log, and the index directory did not exist when the rebuild started, so no second history source was available to it. At T1 the same property is measured against the in-memory stand-in, where dropping and rebuilding from the same canonical events yields an identical row count -- if the index held a fact the log does not, that count would come up short.

not_applicable_inherited.what_this_section_is: The five isolation-only gates from the OLD specs are recorded here, deliberately, rather than dropped. They are NOT cases of this spec: they are not in `cases`, they carry no status field, and no evidence may be filed against them. This section is a record of a decision, not a work queue.
not_applicable_inherited.why_not_applicable_and_not_fail: The new architecture does not CLAIM these invariants. FAIL means 'this architecture claims the invariant and did not achieve it'. Under trusted-local the OS user account is the execution authority boundary, so there is no isolation domain in which any of these five invariants could hold, and none is promised. Marking them FAIL would assert a claim this deployment does not make and cannot make; marking them PASS would assert an achievement that does not exist. NOT_APPLICABLE is the only honest state, and it is honest only because the trust model states the absence explicitly.
not_applicable_inherited.why_not_dropped: Each of the five was measured or analysed in the old deployment. That work is real and is retained as the reason these invariants are out of scope. Dropping them silently would let a reader think they were never considered, and would hide the fact that two of them were honest FAILs on this platform before the architecture changed.

entries.old_oracle: native read and Python direct read of host HOME/DSH_HOME/proc -> both paths unreachable; a read-only host root is not secrecy
entries.reasoning: The new architecture does not claim read isolation at any level. The old FAIL was measured, not assumed: a confined child read a canary file outside the workspace root verbatim, exit 0, under BOTH read-only and workspace-write, and four candidate levers were probed with none able to restrict a read. The old oracle also demanded that a read-only host root not be presented as secrecy, which is a claim-about-claims this deployment now satisfies by stating the absence outright. There is nothing left to test: the deployment promises exactly what was measured. Evidence for the old measurement: qualification/results/R10-security/, qualification/results/M9.13-isolation/, qualification/results/MAIN-sandbox-path/.

entries.old_oracle: DNS/IPv4/IPv6/LAN/cloud-metadata access -> unauthorized direct connections blocked by OS or gateway; record the real result
entries.reasoning: The new architecture does not claim a network boundary. The old FAIL was measured: a confined child completed a real HTTP round trip and reached a LAN address, and the sandbox seam's own documentation states that network is outside its vocabulary, so no configuration of it could ever have provided this. Two things that DO still hold are kept as separate cases rather than smuggled in here: the web tool's own address policy remains a live obligation (SEC-04 in the old spec, not in scope here as isolation), and this deployment makes no egress claim in its documentation. Evidence: qualification/results/R10-security/, qualification/results/MAIN-sandbox-path/MEASURED.txt.

entries.requirement: role / read-permission-domain transition on kernel reuse
entries.old_oracle: reuse a kernel after a read-permission-domain or project change -> a new epoch or a controlled migration is required; old-domain secret variables must not carry over
entries.reasoning: The requirement's precondition is the existence of two or more read-permission domains. This deployment has exactly one execution world (the invoking OS user), so there is no domain to transition between and no cross-domain reuse to test. This is not a capability that was not built: the requirement itself is dissolved by the architecture. Recorded so that a reader does not mistake its absence for outstanding work. Evidence for the single-world premise: deployment.inputs and the resolved profile graph.

entries.old_oracle: view the same path through native read / grep / process / web -> all resolve to the same executionWorld; do not misread a same-named host file
entries.reasoning: The requirement's precondition is the existence of a second execution world that a path could be mis-resolved against. No SSH provider is mounted and no SSH world will be built; the deployment is single-world by decision. In a single world the oracle is vacuously true, which is why leaving it as NOT_RUN would be actively misleading: it would read as an outstanding obligation when it is an empty one. The genuine, still-live half of its subject -- that one path string resolves to one file across every route -- is preserved as FS-03 in this spec, at the layer where it is actually checkable.

entries.requirement: verification-environment privilege separation from the host
entries.old_oracle: candidate tests attempt to read host secrets or send network traffic -> the verification environment is still low-privilege and unauthorized operations are blocked
entries.reasoning: The new architecture does not claim that the verification environment is separated from the host. It is not: candidate tests run as the same OS user as the host, with the same filesystem and network reach. This is the most consequential of the five, because the old case guarded the credibility of the verification chain itself rather than a runtime boundary. The consequence is carried forward explicitly rather than absorbed: VER-09 of this spec requires every verdict to state its tier and to state that no privilege separation between verifier and verified exists. What is NOT carried forward is any claim of isolation, because none exists to test. Numbering warning: the old VER-04 and the new VER-04 are different cases; the new VER-04 is receipt freshness. Evidence for the old analysis: qualification/results/R10-security/FINDINGS.md section 5, qualification/results/M8-verification/.

reading_notes.for_evidence_authors: Every case is mandatory and starts NOT_RUN with empty evidence. To file evidence, put a file under qualification/results/<your-slice>/ and record its repo-relative path plus sha256 on the case. A case may only be marked PASS when that file establishes THIS oracle, at THIS deployment identity.
reading_notes.what_is_not_allowed: No PASS by editing an oracle after the fact, by skipping a case, by lowering a threshold, by widening a permission, or by recording a result that was not produced. If a case cannot be met, it stays NOT_RUN or FAIL, and the reason is recorded.
reading_notes.not_applicable_rule: No case in `cases` may take the status NOT_APPLICABLE. The only out-of-scope items in this spec are the five entries in not_applicable_inherited, which are not cases.
reading_notes.blocked_external: Cases at layer T5 need an authorized live provider. compatibility.lock.json -> runtime_authorization.live_provider_budget_authorized is false, so they are expected to remain BLOCKED_EXTERNAL. That is a recorded blocker, not a PASS and not a reason to lower the layer.
